searchText: https://twitter.com/leoyanzon/status/1559572114872606723?s=20&t=IIKG5-2txTCxagqMqzGSVA i don't have ability to respond in depth here, anyone want to jump in? It's just the way polynomial commitments work, we all agree in a bunch of points to where we will be evaluating our polynomials. And then we can commit to the value of that polynomial on other points without revealing the polynomial. I think his question was about why we need to use the KZG polynomial commitment scheme, because in zcash they use a different polynomial commitment scheme which does not need a trusted setup > Is not possible to extend this to kzg commitments? That looks pretty much like asking if a trusted setup can be avoided in KZG KZG uses a SRS whereas the scheme that zcash uses only needs a CRS You would need a different polynomial commitment scheme, though they have different tradeoffs. I haven't looked at DAS to see exactly why we need KZG though, maybe it can be avoided or maybe there is an additional property apart from homomorphism that is assumed just a heads up, I will be OOO during the call this thursday but will add the main attendees as alternate hosts so everyone can still access the meeting. it will record by default <@550420431744794624> <@405860945018093609> <@427491045308235776> Vitalik wrote about potentially using inner product arguments (IPAs) instead of KZG commitments here: https://ethresear.ch/t/what-would-it-take-to-do-das-with-inner-product-arguments-ipas/12088 IPAs, which is what Halo in zcash uses, does not rely on a trusted setup. thanks for the link, this is very helpful!
